prompt: You are the test author this time: write isCorrect so it accepts a correct Normalizer and rejects broken ones. Complete the checker in the starter file, then run the tests.
explanation: The inputs are chosen so each one can only pass for the right reason. "  Hello   World  " exercises trimming, collapsing and case at once, but a test suite made only of that cannot say which rule an implementation broke -- so "Single" isolates case and "A\tB" isolates the fact that whitespace means more than the space character. An implementation that collapses " +" looks perfect until a tab arrives. The empty and all-whitespace strings are the boundary where a plausible implementation stops returning a value and starts throwing, which is why the calls belong inside try/catch with a crash scored as a failure.
hints: Start with "  Hello   World  " -> "hello world". That one input already fails three of the four broken implementations.
Add an input containing a tab or a newline, not just spaces. An implementation that collapses " +" passes every space-only test and is still wrong.
Wrap every call in one try block ending with `catch (Throwable t) { return false; }`, and check the empty string too.
